characters.description: Sift's ancient companion, capable of consuming energy at extraordinary density. When the Black Pyramid's unstable explosion threatens millions, the tortoise volunteers to help contain it and Sift insists on going too.
characters.name: Sift's elder star tortoise

characters.description: A hostile divine adversary whose agents destabilize the Black Pyramid explosion, creating a threat to millions.
characters.name: Lauquinriel

characters.description: An independent, self-developed person derived from Uru within Ruwen's mental world. She receives carefully limited knowledge from the goddess, teaches Ruwen an advanced form of spirit casting, and takes Uru's appearance for his public plan.
characters.name: The inner-world Uru avatar

characters.description: Five hostile infiltrators concealed among the manipulated fighters approaching Eiru. They remain standing after Uru's projected sacrifice breaks much of the crowd's control, exposing the apparent invasion as a coordinated ambush.
characters.name: The five Aspects

characters.description: One of five deities who join Lauquinriel in a direct attack after the confrontation with the Aspects. Haffa arrives as part of a peak-divine coalition facing Ruwen near the vulnerable civilian force.
characters.name: Haffa

characters.description: One of the five deities accompanying Lauquinriel in the assault on Eiru. Quentin is part of the hostile coalition that appears after the Aspects are confronted.
characters.name: Quentin

characters.description: A member of Lauquinriel's divine coalition, arriving with four other deities to attack Ruwen while thousands of civilians remain nearby.
characters.name: Isaac

characters.description: One of the deities in Lauquinriel's attacking coalition. Noctos joins the direct confrontation that follows the hidden Aspect assault.
characters.name: Noctos

characters.description: One of the deities allied with Lauquinriel in the direct attack on Eiru. Wenquian appears as part of the six-deity force confronting Ruwen.
characters.name: Wenquian

recaps.ending: Ruwen returns to Eiru as a Divine apostate able to perceive and alter the Eighth Harmony. Uru's projected sacrifice frees most of the 53,000 fighters from manipulation, exposing the five Aspects hidden among them. Ruwen and the 29 golden warriors destroy the Aspect bearers, but War's allies extract Gundr and the critically wounded Lylan. Lauquinriel then arrives with five deities. Ruwen moves the third temple into the battle, Xavier absorbs their combined attack, Hamma shields the civilians, Rami disrupts the attackers, and Overlord's forces contain the demons. Haffa and Quentin die. Isaac escapes with severe damage, while Noctos and Wenquian also retreat. Lauquinriel gets away carrying Nameless and is probably dead afterward, though this is not confirmed. Hamma tends the surviving Xavier, and Big D helps send the former invaders home. Ruwen commits to political reform and a replacement for the broken Pact. His urgent unresolved tasks are finding Lylan and Gundr, learning whether Sift and the elder star tortoise contained the Black Pyramid explosion, and preventing the imprisoned darkness from escaping.
recaps.in_short: Ruwen Starfield returns to a politically fractured Eiru while his failing soul prison and the divine shard in his mind make revival unsafe. He restrains a merchant-led revolt, rebuilds his backup, reconciles Uru with her shard, and survives a planned death before using Hamma's wishes to become the first Divine apostate. His new perception reveals the Eighth Harmony and greatly expands his Architect authority. Back in Eiru, a manipulated army conceals five Aspects while the Black Pyramid faces catastrophic failure. Ruwen's allies protect the civilians and destroy the Aspects, but War escapes with the wounded Lylan and Gundr. Six deities then attack. Ruwen kills Haffa and Quentin, cripples Isaac, and drives Isaac, Noctos, and Wenquian away, while Lauquinriel escapes with Nameless and may die afterward. The battle ends, but Sift and the elder star tortoise remain missing at the Black Pyramid, Lylan is lost, the Pact is broken, and Eiru must be rebuilt.

recaps.text: Previously: Ruwen Starfield became Eiru's Architect and champion while gathering allies with distinct roles in his expanding responsibilities. Rami shares his mental world, where Overlord exists as an independent counterpart and a separate divine shard of Uru has found shelter. Hamma is Ruwen's partner, a chapel priestess, and a healer. Sift is his martial companion, while Lylan serves as a scout. Lear manages the third temple and its systems, and Fractal pursues difficult research from his lair. Blapy remains a powerful ally connected to unusual dimensional spaces. Together, these companions form the political, spiritual, martial, and technical support around Ruwen as his authority in Eiru grows.

So far this book: Ruwen returns to Midpoint in disguise and finds Uru's lands in crisis. Free class choice has disrupted labor, training, and public order, while hostility between northern residents and revived southerners is growing. Big D shows him that abrupt reform and his long absence helped create the instability. Her counsel also forces him to reconsider a plan to answer resistance with overwhelming violence. On the way to Eiru, Rami discovers that a frightened pilot was coerced into identifying Ruwen. Ruwen protects the man's family, then defeats the merchant organizer's ambush without killing its members. He warns that another attack will end his restraint. Lear helps him plan tests for abilities he cannot safely power with spirit, but Ruwen's damaged soul and the divine fragment inside him make revival dangerous. Reunited with Hamma after eighteen months, he finally describes the Savage Island disaster, where twenty-nine companions died. Hamma helps him begin separating grief for those people from his belief that every death was his fault.

Ruwen tests whether the third temple's mana can replace spirit for his powers and gives Uru's fragment a temporary body, but the experiment does not solve his deteriorating soul shell. Lear is already using nearly all available storage to preserve 200,000 children, and Ruwen may lose everything gained since his old backup if revival becomes necessary. His former mentor says Ruwen's parents were sent on an untraceable assignment to protect someone and warns that an infernal lord seeks two journals connected to a soul vault. The mentor also reinforces Big D's lesson that durable reform needs participation rather than command. As Eiru's council gathers, Ruwen stages a political deception: Overlord takes his appearance while Ruwen presents himself as Uru's shadow. Rami discovers that the opposing merchant king is the historical masked bard, a performer able to manipulate emotion through sound. Appearing before the divided faithful, Ruwen publicly orders them to withdraw and thereby establishes that Uru's shadow and Ruwen are separate figures. The display may avert religious war, but the merchant king's expected attack remains imminent.

The merchant king's assassins attack after Ruwen's public performance, but Ruwen's allies defeat the ambush and invade the king's underground headquarters. Ruwen captures him alive. Rami's memory reading exposes his plan to seize Uru's territory, mine Tyrium, and hire the infernal lord to destroy the gods. She also finds that Lylan descends from his lost family. That connection leads Ruwen to offer him a day to redirect his organization toward stability instead of revolt, then release him. Ruwen next enters his rapidly expanding mental world. It has become a city of nearly independent people whose faith in him provides social order and may also be worsening the pressure on his soul. Nameless, a nihilistic construct, demands the freedom to leave for the infernal lord. Ruwen refuses because releasing it could endanger his mind, creating a conflict between his promise of choice and his duty to protect the inner population. Elsewhere in that world, he discovers a sealed maple grove containing 29 golden forms of the fallen Bamboo Vipers around the refuge created by an earlier secrecy oath.

Ruwen pauses the larger crises to rejoin Hamma, Sift, Lylan, and the Deepwell workers. Tora transfers the ceremonial Baby Band title to him, beginning an initiation built around Bandball, inventory games, and magically intensified drinking. Hamma repeatedly heals him, while Bliz introduces the customs and defeats him in a record Bandball match. The worker gathering restores a sense of community and directs its gambling proceeds toward assistance for people in need. During the Blind Bandit game, Ruwen selects a strange living egg from Bliz's inventory. Lylan feels compelled toward it and hears a distant, sea-like call. A two-headed winged hydra hatches in her hands, bites both palms without leaving injury or poison, and then disappears beyond Ruwen's ability to detect it. Ruwen tells her what Lear and Rami have established: she and her brother descend directly from Gundr and a southern queen. The creature appears to have answered that lineage, but neither its location nor what its appearance has done to Lylan is yet known.

Hamma offers her three extraordinary wishes for Ruwen's mission and the pair commit to a more trusting relationship. She also identifies Archie, the being in her necklace whom she can understand clearly. Rami has reconciled with Xavier, while the attempt to build a godstone still fails because an inorganic vessel cannot hold a soul. Ruwen tests civic incentives in his inner city as a possible model for repairing Eiru. The merchant king pauses his uprising but refuses cooperation, and he rejects Lylan when told she is his distant descendant. Northern war rallies continue under coordinated outside influence. Fractal's ability to perceive vibration helps Ruwen connect music with stored identity, and meditation with Sift lets him hear the structured harmony of Sift's soul. A second crisis then presses in: Blapy warns that the stored explosion is worsening and initially argues that Ruwen must die to move it safely. Fractal and Lear propose a harmonic crystal matrix that could expand the third temple's storage enough to preserve Ruwen instead. Ruwen reveals Harmony to Blapy, forcing her briefly into a human divine form and proving the technique can constrain even her.

Ruwen trades his method of Harmony to Blapy for spiritual healing and a recipe Fractal can study. Fractal's resonance crystals successfully expand the third temple's storage, creating a path to synchronize Ruwen's enormous inner world. The backup cannot preserve divine structures, however, so death would erase Uru's shard. Ruwen brings Uru into his mind despite the danger. Uru confirms that Ruwen's parents are alive and guarding one of Penn's hidden aura experiments, then confronts the shard he has protected. Uru accepts her as a separate person, and together they devise a brief transfer into an external container during Ruwen's death. The arrangement is dangerous but makes survival possible. A relic fortune golem calls Ruwen the conductor of the Eighth Harmony and warns of several coming disasters. Rami proposes that a controlled death could also let him become a composer and gain the musical knowledge needed for Harmony. Finally, Hamma uses her first wish to compel answers from Uru. They learn that souls can level, that Sift already possesses a higher-level soul, and that revealing the method could encourage mass murder by anyone seeking to steal soul aura.

Uru confirms that Lylan carries Hydra heritage and is the surviving queen of an old sea-bound matriarchy. Archie is revealed as the living anchor holding Uru's concealed divine realm together. More urgently, the damaged Black Pyramid contains the Dark Priest and infected archangels behind eight gates. The prisoner can consume matter and spirit, and the disrupted soul field raises the prospect of their escape. Uru's hidden realm offers extreme time dilation, enough for Ruwen and Sift to attempt long transitions while only hours pass outside, but Ruwen must first survive becoming the first Divine apostate. After healing his spiritual system and completing a current backup, Ruwen deliberately dies in the third temple's revival bath. Uru temporarily holds her shard outside his mind. He revives seven seconds later with his mental world intact and safely takes the shard back. Ruwen exchanges his fighter path for merchant, crafter, and composer training, gaining the harmonic knowledge he sought. His soul prison is still near failure, and the apparent success is immediately overshadowed when Hamma senses a new emergency at the Black Pyramid.

Enemies breached the Black Pyramid's lower vaults during Ruwen's controlled death, nearly causing planetary destruction. Hamma spends her remaining wishes on the fastest available transition elixirs for Ruwen and Sift and on access to Uru's time-dilated realm. Hamma and Lylan leave to investigate the breach while Ruwen, Sift, and Rami begin transformations that take centuries from their perspective. Sift reaches early sapphire and guards Ruwen through a far longer process in which Ruwen's body disintegrates and reforms. Ruwen awakens at the first Divine level. His transition destroys the prison around his soul, damages the remote realm, and leaves his inner constructs rebuilding, but his companions survive. His strengthened bond lets Rami draw upon his inner energies. Divine perception exposes the fundamental note-sigils of the world and the previously hidden eighth harmony. His Architect authority also expands from planetary to solar-system scale, accompanied by warnings of corrupted systems and a failed universe lookup. Ruwen begins learning to shape his soul and alter the environment, while he and Rami fear that further experimentation could alert hostile gods or a larger multiversal authority.

Ruwen returns to the third temple and finds two simultaneous emergencies. Lauquinriel's agents have destabilized the Black Pyramid explosion, and more than 53,000 manipulated fighters are marching into Eiru. Sift and his elder star tortoise leave to consume the explosion, with no assurance they will survive. Archie recovers Ruwen's missing apocalypse hoop, including valuable research journals, but the approaching army takes priority. Ruwen deploys with Hamma, Lylan, Rami, Xavier, Overlord, and an independent Uru-derived avatar. Their performance shows the crowd Uru's sacrifice during the earlier apocalypse, breaking much of the emotional control. Five Aspects remain standing among them and attack. Lylan intercepts War's strike against Gundr and is critically wounded. A dimensional mage extracts all three, leaving Lylan alive but beyond Lear's reach. Ruwen kills the replacement Drought and binds the other Aspects with Harmony. He then manifests the 29 golden Bamboo Vipers from his inner sanctuary. They permanently destroy Pestilence, Plague, Poison, and War. The victory is immediately eclipsed by the arrival of Lauquinriel and five other deities.

The six-deity assault forces Ruwen to honor Nameless's demand for freedom. He transfers the construct to Lauquinriel before a neutral witness and restores a copy only after the transfer is verified, preserving the integrity of his promise. Lauquinriel escapes Ruwen's strike while carrying Nameless, and the outcome for both remains uncertain. Ruwen declares the old Pact ended and pulls Uru's third temple hundreds of miles to the battlefield, gaining the mana needed for the remaining fight. Xavier absorbs the combined energy attack of five deities and vents it safely with the Uru avatar's help. Hamma uses Prayer 12 to shield roughly 50,000 civilians, Rami disrupts the coalition mentally, and Overlord's minions engage the demon horde. Ruwen kills Haffa and Quentin, severely damages Isaac, and drives Isaac, Noctos, and Wenquian back to their realms. The Uru avatar destroys the demons that breach the line, and Hamma begins healing the exhausted Xavier. Ruwen sends the former invaders home to mourn and promises political change. He now faces Eiru's reconstruction, a replacement for the Pact, the search for Lylan and Gundr, and the unknown fate of Sift and the elder star tortoise at the Black Pyramid.

characters.description: A Five from Carolina and one of the six Elite, the public's sentimental favorite to become princess. She has admitted to herself that she loves Maxon but will not commit to him, partly because she doubts she could ever be the kind of woman a throne requires and partly because Aspen, the boy she loved at home, now serves in the palace guard and she sees him daily. She is blunt, quick-tempered, and increasingly angry about the caste system she has begun to see clearly from the inside.
characters.name: America Singer

characters.description: The crown prince of Illéa, who must choose a wife from the six remaining girls. His friendship with America has become the most important relationship in his life, but he is losing patience with her refusal to decide, and his father is steering him toward a more suitable choice. He is far more constrained than he appears: the King controls what he is told, what he may announce, and whom he is permitted to favor.
characters.name: Maxon Schreave

characters.description: America's first love, a Six drafted into the army and posted to the palace as a guard. He is assigned to the floor where the Selected live, which puts him within reach of her most nights, and he has not accepted that their relationship is finished. Discovery would be treated as treason for both of them.
characters.name: Aspen Leger

characters.description: One of the Elite and America's closest friend at the palace, a Four whose warmth has made her the country's favorite. She has grown noticeably quieter on the subject of Maxon than a front-runner ought to be, and she deflects America's questions about it.
characters.name: Marlee Tames

characters.description: A Two and a model, the most openly ruthless of the Elite. She works the cameras, manipulates the other girls, and pursues Maxon aggressively, and she is not above circulating a story about a rival to damage her.
characters.name: Celeste Newsome

characters.description: A Three among the Elite, gracious, composed, and genuinely interested in what the crown could do for the country. She is America's friendliest rival and, as the field narrows, her most serious one.
characters.name: Kriss Ambers

characters.description: One of the Elite, quiet and watchful, with family connections abroad that make her useful to a court managing a long war on Illéa's western border. She competes carefully rather than openly.
characters.name: Elise Whisks

characters.description: One of the Elite, cheerful, chatty, and largely untroubled by the competition. She is close to her younger sister at home and talks about her often.
characters.name: Natalie Luca

characters.description: The king of Illéa, who has decided that America is unsuitable and works steadily to remove her: managing what his son hears, controlling what the girls may say on air, and setting the court against her. He is considerably harsher in private than the broadcasts suggest.
characters.name: King Clarkson Schreave

characters.description: The queen of Illéa, who won a Selection herself as a Four and is the gentlest presence at court. She is fond of America and quietly sympathetic to the girls, but she does not contradict her husband.
characters.name: Queen Amberly Schreave

characters.description: One of America's maids, small, nervous, and wholly devoted to her. She is easily frightened, particularly by the rebel raids, and America looks out for her.
characters.name: Lucy

characters.description: A palace guard, well-liked among the officers, who is discovered to have been secretly involved with one of the Selected. Under Illéan law that is a capital offense against the crown, and he is punished publicly and stripped of his caste.
characters.name: Carter Woodwork

characters.description: The founder of Illéa, revered in the official histories as the man who held the country together after the wars and gave it the caste system. His private journals, kept in the palace and read by very few people, describe how he actually came to power and what the castes were designed to do.
characters.name: Gregory Illéa

recaps.ending: America's unsanctioned broadcast about dismantling the castes costs her the King's tolerance and, for a time, Maxon's trust; he spends the following weeks with Kriss and Celeste and refuses to reassure her. Rebel violence escalates, Natalie's younger sister is killed, and the household is badly shaken. America finally admits to herself that her hesitation has been fear rather than doubt. She goes to Maxon, tells him she wants him, and asks to stay rather than for an answer she has not earned; he agrees to keep her in the Selection without promising her anything. Five girls remain: America, Kriss, Celeste, Natalie, and Elise. Marlee and Carter, publicly caned and reduced to the lowest caste, are living quietly inside the palace as servants under Maxon's protection, and America knows it. Maxon knows what his father's private histories actually contain, and that the country's founding story is a fabrication. The King is now working openly to have America removed. Aspen, meanwhile, has begun turning his attention to Lucy, one of America's maids, loosening the hold he has had on her. The Selection goes on with America committed to it for the first time.
recaps.in_short: Six girls remain in the Selection. America is the public's favorite and Maxon's, but she cannot choose between him and Aspen, who now serves in the palace guard. When her friend Marlee is caught with a guard, the two are publicly caned and stripped of their castes, and America's faith in the palace collapses. She learns that Maxon is beaten by his own father, and that Illéa's official history is a lie: Gregory Illéa's private journals show that he engineered his rise and built the castes to entrench it. Emboldened, America uses a live broadcast to announce a plan to dismantle the caste system that the King never approved. Her standing collapses, Maxon turns to the other girls, and rebel attacks grow deadlier, killing Natalie's sister. By the end America has decided what she wants: she tells Maxon she is committed to him and asks to stay, and he agrees to give her another chance, with the King now openly working to remove her and Marlee living secretly in the palace as a servant.

recaps.text: Previously: Illéa sorts its people into eight numbered castes. America Singer, a Five from Carolina, entered the Selection only because her mother insisted and because Aspen, the Six she loved in secret, ended their relationship rather than hold her back. Her name was drawn, and at the palace she told Prince Maxon on their first night that she did not want him. He kept her anyway, as a friend who would tell him the truth about his country, and what she told him about hunger and the castes began to change how he thought about governing. She became the public's favorite and, against her intentions, fell in love with him. Before she could say so she discovered Aspen serving in the palace guard, drafted out of his caste and posted to Angeles. Rebel raids on the palace grew steadily more violent, and America worked out that two different groups were behind them, one bent on destruction and the other apparently searching the building for something. The Selection was then cut to its final six, the Elite: America, Marlee, Celeste, Kriss, Natalie, and Elise.

Six girls remain, and the scrutiny tightens: the Elite are given more responsibility, more airtime, and more instruction in what a princess is expected to be. America is now certain she loves Maxon and equally certain she is not what the throne wants, and she keeps refusing to commit. Aspen, posted to her floor, presses her to remember what she promised him, and every meeting risks both their lives. King Clarkson makes no secret of his contempt for her, restricting what she may say on air and steering Maxon toward the other girls. Outside the palace the war on Illéa's western border grinds on and rebel raids grow more frequent, so the household lives with the safe room always in mind.

The palace discovers that Marlee has been secretly involved with a guard, Carter Woodwork. Because a Selected girl belongs to the prince until he releases her, the two are treated as traitors: they are publicly caned in the palace courtyard while the household is made to watch, stripped of their castes, and removed. America tries to stop it and is dragged away. The punishment destroys her remaining faith in the palace and, for a time, in Maxon, who did not prevent it. Her closest friend is gone, and she can no longer pretend that the rules she is living under are anything but brutal.

Estranged from Maxon, America turns back toward Aspen, and the risk the two of them are running becomes far more real to her after what happened to Marlee. The palace closes ranks and behaves as though the caning were an ordinary matter of law, which it is. The Elite are each set to prepare a public project showing what they would do with the position of princess, and America begins to think seriously about what she would want to change rather than about how to survive the competition. She also begins to understand that the cruelty she has seen is not incidental to how the country is run.

America sees the scars across Maxon's back and learns that the King has beaten him for years, which reframes everything about how he behaves in his father's presence. Maxon then takes her into the palace's private collection and shows her the records the royal family keeps to itself, including Gregory Illéa's own journals. The founding story every Illéan is taught is a fabrication: Illéa maneuvered himself into power during the collapse and designed the caste system to lock it in place for his descendants. America also learns that the Northern rebels have been raiding the palace to reach these records rather than to kill, and that they want the truth made public. Separately she discovers that Marlee and Carter are alive and living inside the palace as servants, kept there quietly with Maxon's help. What she now knows makes the castes look less like tradition and more like a deliberate arrangement that could be undone.

Given a live broadcast to present her project, America goes off the approved script and announces a plan to dismantle the caste system, something the King never sanctioned. The country reacts, but the palace reacts harder: Clarkson is enraged, her standing collapses, and only her popularity keeps her from being sent home outright. Maxon, blindsided and furious that she acted without him, pulls away and spends his time with Kriss and Celeste, while Celeste works the situation to her own advantage. America is left isolated, uncertain whether the risk was worth it, and no longer able to assume Maxon will choose her.

Rebel attacks grow deadlier and reach beyond the palace; Natalie's younger sister is killed, and the household's sense of safety goes with her. America finally recognizes that her hesitation has been fear rather than genuine doubt. She goes to Maxon, tells him she wants him and is prepared to fight his father for it, and asks him to keep her in the Selection rather than to promise her anything. He agrees to give her another chance. Five girls remain, Marlee and Carter are living in the palace under Maxon's protection, the King is working openly to remove America, and Aspen has begun turning his attention toward her maid Lucy.

characters.description: The bitter ruler of the Nomes beneath the earth. Still angry over his earlier defeat by Ozma and Dorothy, he wants his Magic Belt back and begins planning to conquer Oz by attacking from below.
characters.name: The Nome King

characters.description: Dorothy's hardworking uncle in Kansas. A mortgage now threatens the farm he rebuilt after the cyclone, leaving him ashamed that years of labor may end without a home for the family.
characters.name: Uncle Henry

characters.description: Dorothy's loving aunt, whose life in Kansas has been shaped by hard work and worry. She faces the loss of the farm with Uncle Henry and is cautious about Dorothy's promise of a secure life in fairyland.
characters.name: Aunt Em

characters.description: A Kansas girl whose repeated adventures have made her a friend of Ozma and many inhabitants of Oz. Learning that the family farm will be lost, she hopes at last to bring Aunt Em and Uncle Henry into the safety of Oz.
characters.name: Dorothy Gale

characters.description: The young ruler of Oz and Dorothy's close friend. She offers Dorothy's family a permanent home in the Emerald City and tries to govern her peaceful country without fear or cruelty.
characters.name: Ozma

characters.description: The Nome King's highest general, chosen to organize the invasion of Oz. Clever, boastful, and untrustworthy, he proposes a tunnel beneath the Deadly Desert and seeks powerful allies for the attack.
characters.name: Guph

characters.description: The immense leader of the Whimsies, whose people wear large pasteboard heads because their natural heads are very small. He agrees to join Guph's invasion in hope of taking part of Oz.
characters.name: Chief Whimsie

characters.description: A huge but courteous beast who is one of Dorothy's oldest friends. Aunt Em initially fears him, but his gentle conduct soon shows that his alarming appearance does not make him dangerous to friends.
characters.name: The Cowardly Lion

characters.description: The proud, enormous ruler of the Growleywogs. He offers his fierce warriors to Guph's alliance but expects his people, not the Nomes, to claim the richest rewards after victory.
characters.name: Grand Gallipoot

characters.description: An Highly Magnified and thoroughly educated insect who runs Oz's college. He welcomes Uncle Henry and Aunt Em during their tour and proudly explains the unusual education offered there.
characters.name: The Woggle-Bug

characters.description: The mysterious leader of the Phanfasms, powerful shape-changing spirits whom even Guph finds frightening. He permits the alliance because the Phanfasms enjoy causing harm and confusion.
characters.name: The First and Foremost

characters.description: Dorothy's old friend, now living in the Emerald City and studying real magic. He accompanies Dorothy and Toto on a tour of Oz's remarkable communities.
characters.name: The Wizard

characters.description: Dorothy's small black dog. In Oz he can speak if he chooses, though he generally remains happiest following Dorothy and investigating each new place with her.
characters.name: Toto

characters.description: Dorothy's old companion, made of straw and valued for his unusual wisdom. When Oz faces an invading army too powerful to defeat by force, he searches for a peaceful plan that can protect everyone.
characters.name: The Scarecrow

recaps.ending: Ozma learns that the Nome King and his allies are about to enter Oz through their completed tunnel, but she refuses to answer invasion with killing. The Scarecrow devises a defense using the Forbidden Fountain, whose enchanted water removes the drinker's memories. The invaders emerge in the Emerald City, drink, and forget their anger, their identities, and their plan of conquest. Ozma treats them kindly and sends the harmless armies home, with the transformed alliance no longer threatening her people. Glinda then uses magic to make Oz invisible and unreachable to the outside world, preventing future armies or ordinary visitors from finding it. Dorothy, Aunt Em, and Uncle Henry remain secure in the Emerald City as permanent residents. Before communication closes, Dorothy sends one final message explaining that Oz will no longer be open to reports from the outside world.
recaps.in_short: When Uncle Henry's mortgaged Kansas farm is about to be lost, Ozma brings Dorothy, Aunt Em, and Uncle Henry to live permanently in the Emerald City. While the newcomers tour Oz's many curious settlements, the vengeful Nome King orders General Guph to dig beneath the Deadly Desert and recruit the Whimsies, Growleywogs, and Phanfasms for an invasion. Ozma learns of the threat but refuses to fight a deadly battle. Instead, the Scarecrow arranges for the attackers to drink enchanted water from the Forbidden Fountain. They forget their wicked purpose and are sent peacefully home. Glinda then makes Oz invisible and closes it to the outside world. Dorothy and her family remain safely with their friends, while the Nome King's attempt to conquer Oz ends without bloodshed.

recaps.text: Dorothy Gale has traveled repeatedly between Kansas and Oz, becoming the close friend of Ozma, the country's young ruler. Dorothy and her companions once defeated the Nome King and took his powerful Magic Belt. The belt now belongs to Ozma, while Dorothy still lives in Kansas with Aunt Em and Uncle Henry and visits Oz only through magic.

The Nome King remains furious that Dorothy and Ozma defeated him and carried away his Magic Belt. He appoints Guph to prepare an invasion of Oz through a tunnel under the Deadly Desert. In Kansas, Uncle Henry reveals that the bank will take the mortgaged farm, leaving the family without a home. Dorothy asks Ozma for help, and Ozma brings Dorothy, Aunt Em, and Uncle Henry to the Emerald City as permanent residents. While Dorothy's family begins meeting the strange but friendly citizens of Oz, Guph recruits the Whimsies, whose small natural heads are hidden inside enormous false ones, to join the Nome army.

Aunt Em overcomes her fear of the Cowardly Lion, and she and Uncle Henry tour Oz, including the Woggle-Bug's unusual college. Guph continues gathering dangerous allies. The proud Growleywogs agree to fight but secretly intend to take Oz for themselves. The shape-changing Phanfasms also join, frightening even the Nome general; they too plan to betray their partners after the conquest. Guph reports success to the Nome King while work on the underground tunnel continues. Elsewhere, Dorothy and the Wizard set out to visit more of Oz, unaware of the army preparing beneath the desert.

Dorothy, the Wizard, and their companions wander among Oz's curious settlements. They meet people who make long, useless speeches, the paper Cuttenclips, the mixed-up Fuddles, the kitchen-tool citizens of Utensia, and the edible inhabitants of Bunbury. In Bunnybury, a town built for rabbits, Dorothy helps its king understand that royal duties and a comfortable home matter more than running away. The travelers later pass the anxious Flutterbudgets. As they return, the Tin Woodman brings news that a vast hostile army is approaching from beneath the country, and Ozma's peaceful kingdom prepares for the danger.

Ozma learns the full invasion plan but refuses to save Oz through slaughter. The Scarecrow proposes using the enchanted water of the Forbidden Fountain, which removes the memories of anyone who drinks it. The Nome King, Guph, and their allied Whimsies, Growleywogs, and Phanfasms march through the completed tunnel into the Emerald City. Thirsty from the journey, they drink from the fountain and forget their identities, grudges, and plans. Ozma sends the now harmless invaders home. To prevent another attack, Glinda makes Oz invisible and closes its borders to the outside world. Dorothy, Aunt Em, and Uncle Henry remain in the Emerald City, where the threatened loss of their Kansas farm can no longer separate the family or leave them homeless.

characters.description: An Araluen knight visiting Nihon-Ja to observe the country's warrior traditions. Horace's ability and direct sense of duty draw him into the danger surrounding Emperor Shigeru when a study journey becomes a rebellion.
characters.name: Horace Altman

characters.description: One of Horace's childhood companions from the Redmont Ward, now trained in law, languages and administration. George accompanies the Nihon-Jan visit in a diplomatic capacity and lacks Horace's fighting experience, but he can carry information and negotiate where a warrior cannot.
characters.name: George Carter

characters.description: The ruler of Nihon-Ja. Shigeru respects ability more than inherited rank and wants the powerful warrior class to accept obligations toward the common people, a position that has earned both deep loyalty and dangerous opposition.
characters.name: Emperor Shigeru

characters.description: The Emperor's cousin and a loyal Senshi warrior. Shukin knows the country's customs, terrain and military hierarchy and helps protect Shigeru when the imperial party can no longer rely on rank alone.
characters.name: Shukin

characters.description: A senior Senshi lord with a large military following. Arisaka rejects Shigeru's effort to limit the privileges of the warrior class and commands enough support to turn political resistance into an armed challenge.
characters.name: Arisaka

characters.description: A full Ranger and Horace's closest friend. When news of the rebellion reaches the Araluens, Will brings tracking, archery and an instinct for adapting familiar tools to an unfamiliar kind of war.
characters.name: Will

characters.description: Will's former mentor and one of Araluen's most experienced Rangers. Halt joins the effort to find Horace and approaches Nihon-Jan weapons and tactics as practical problems rather than obstacles imposed by custom.
characters.name: Halt

characters.description: King Duncan's daughter and heir. Cassandra knows Horace as both a trusted friend and the man whose absence matters to her personally, and she is prepared to use her royal authority to organise a journey after him.
characters.name: Princess Cassandra

characters.description: An Araluen Courier and Will's partner. Alyss brings diplomatic training, calm judgement and the ability to read motives to the expedition searching for Horace.
characters.name: Alyss Mainwaring

characters.description: A Skandian skirl whose crew has aided Will before. Gundar is a seasoned captain in dangerous seas and provides the long-distance transport needed to reach Nihon-Ja.
characters.name: Gundar Hardstriker

characters.description: An Arridi military commander and ally of the Araluens since Erak's rescue. Selethen's experience with foreign courts and organised troops adds another perspective to a mission far beyond any participant's home territory.
characters.name: Selethen

characters.description: The farming and forestry people who form much of Nihon-Ja's common population. They have little of the Senshi class's armour or formal training, but their knowledge of the land and loyalty to Shigeru give the Emperor a force from which resistance can be built.
characters.name: The Kikori

recaps.ending: Shigeru's Kikori force holds together against Arisaka's Senshi because Horace has given ordinary workers a disciplined formation that can resist individually superior warriors. Will, Halt and their companions add ranged weapons, fieldcraft and tactical changes suited to the enemy's armour. Loyal Senshi join the Emperor, and Arisaka is defeated and killed in the decisive fighting. Shigeru is restored as the acknowledged Emperor rather than becoming a dependent figure protected by foreign visitors. The Kikori have demonstrated courage and military value that the old hierarchy denied them, strengthening Shigeru's effort to govern across class divisions and curb the Senshi's inherited privileges. The surviving Araluens and their allies reunite after the long separation. Horace and Cassandra are open about the bond that drew her across the world to find him, while Will and Alyss remain together after tensions caused by the journey. George's warning and Gundar and Selethen's help have all contributed to the rescue. With the rebellion ended and Shigeru secure, the visitors leave Nihon-Ja for home.
recaps.in_short: Horace and George are visiting Nihon-Ja when the Senshi lord Arisaka rebels against Emperor Shigeru's reforms. Horace stays with the Emperor while George carries warning away. Shigeru, his cousin Shukin and a shrinking band of loyalists flee toward remote country; Shukin dies buying them time. In Araluen, Cassandra, Alyss, Will and Halt organise a rescue, aided on the voyage by Gundar Hardstriker and Selethen. Horace reaches a hidden Kikori community and turns farmers and woodsmen into a disciplined infantry force, adapting the Skandian shield wall so they can withstand heavily trained Senshi. The rescue party eventually joins him and contributes Ranger archery, improvised weapons and wider military experience. In the final battle, Shigeru's mixed force defeats the rebellion and Arisaka is killed. The Emperor returns to power with the Kikori's courage publicly established. Horace and Cassandra acknowledge their love, and the reunited companions begin the journey home.

recaps.text: Previously: Will trained as a Ranger under Halt and became one of Horace's closest friends. Together they helped defeat Morgarath, survived the conflict in Skandia and later protected Araluen from threats at Macindaw. Will and the Courier Alyss acknowledged their love after she was rescued from Keren. Princess Cassandra, who travelled under the name Evanlyn during her captivity with Will, is King Duncan's heir and has developed a close bond with Horace. The friends also gained allies abroad, including the Skandian captain Gundar Hardstriker and the Arridi commander Selethen. Most recently, Will, Halt and Horace broke the Outsiders' power in Clonmel and pursued Tennyson until his movement was destroyed. Horace has since travelled to the distant country of Nihon-Ja with George Carter, another former Redmont ward, as part of a visit intended for study and diplomacy rather than war.

Horace and George are guests in Nihon-Ja, where Horace studies the methods and discipline of the Senshi warrior class. Emperor Shigeru takes an interest in the Araluen knight because Horace treats rank as a responsibility rather than a licence to dominate others. Shigeru has been pressing the same principle in his own government, seeking fairer treatment for common people and less automatic privilege for powerful Senshi lords. That policy has created serious opposition. The visit changes character as reports of unrest gather around Arisaka, a senior lord with enough armed retainers and allied houses to challenge the Emperor rather than merely argue with him.

Arisaka's opposition becomes open rebellion. Shigeru is away from the strongest centres of imperial power and cannot assume that every Senshi commander will honour his title. Horace chooses to remain with him, judging that leaving a threatened host would violate both friendship and duty. Shigeru's cousin Shukin organises the immediate defence and guides the reduced party away from forces trying to capture or kill the Emperor. George is better suited to carrying news than to a running fight, so the companions' survival also depends on warning reaching people who can bring help. The fugitives move toward country where Arisaka's armoured warriors cannot use their numbers as easily.

Shigeru's party is repeatedly pressed by the rebel pursuit. Shukin stays behind at a critical point to delay Arisaka's warriors and is killed, giving the Emperor and Horace the time they need to escape. They reach a remote Kikori community whose farmers and woodsmen are loyal to Shigeru but have neither the equipment nor the status of Senshi. Horace sees that they cannot become expert swordsmen quickly enough to meet Arisaka on his terms. He begins looking for a formation that will let disciplined groups survive against individually superior fighters. Elsewhere, George's warning sets a rescue in motion: Cassandra, Alyss, Will and Halt commit themselves to finding Horace and the displaced Emperor.

Horace adapts the shield-wall methods he learned from the Skandians, training the Kikori to hold close ranks and combine simple weapons so that Senshi cannot defeat them one at a time. Their work ethic and trust in Shigeru begin to turn a refuge into an army. The Emperor also seeks loyal Senshi who will oppose Arisaka without abandoning the reforms that caused the rebellion. The Araluen rescue party makes the long voyage with help from Gundar Hardstriker and Selethen, surviving the hazards of unfamiliar seas and reaching Nihon-Ja with little certainty about Horace's location. Will and Halt then apply Ranger tracking to connect scattered reports of the rebellion with the route taken by Shigeru's party.

The searchers reunite with Horace and Shigeru's supporters. The Kikori can now manoeuvre as a body, but Arisaka still has more trained warriors, better armour and confidence that commoners will break when charged. Will and Halt study how to interrupt that advantage with concentrated archery and improvised battlefield devices, while Selethen and Gundar contribute experience from very different kinds of fighting. Cassandra and Alyss help hold the alliance together around Shigeru's legitimate authority. The coming battle is designed not to imitate Senshi warfare but to force Arisaka against a combination he has not prepared for: a stable infantry wall, missiles capable of threatening armour and loyal Senshi willing to stand beside the Kikori.

Arisaka commits his Senshi against Shigeru's mixed force, expecting the Kikori to scatter. Horace's training holds: the close formation absorbs the assault while Ranger archery and adapted weapons reduce the rebels' advantage in armour. Loyal Senshi support the Emperor, and the battle turns against the coup. Arisaka is defeated and killed, ending the immediate challenge to Shigeru's rule. The Emperor is restored with new evidence that courage and service are not confined to a hereditary warrior class; the Kikori who protected him have earned public honour and a place in the settlement that follows. Horace is reunited with the friends who crossed the world to find him. He and Cassandra acknowledge their love, Will and Alyss remain together, and George, Gundar and Selethen share in the successful rescue. With Nihon-Ja secure under Shigeru, the visitors prepare to return home.

characters.description: A Forger from MaiPon: an artist who carves stamps that rewrite an object's history, so that a cracked window becomes one that was never broken, provided the invented history is plausible enough for the object to accept it. In the Rose Empire the art is considered blasphemy and its practitioners are executed. Shai is caught in the imperial palace after replacing a priceless artefact with a copy of her own making, and is imprisoned to await execution. She is proud of her craft, contemptuous of people who call it fraud, and already working on an escape before anyone offers her a bargain.
characters.name: Shai

characters.description: One of the emperor's arbiters, elderly, austere and the least self-serving member of the council. He regards Forgery as theft dressed up as art and Shai as a criminal who should have been executed, but he is the one assigned to review her work day by day, and he is capable of changing his mind when the evidence requires it.
characters.name: Gaotona

characters.description: The head of the arbiters' council and the most powerful of the emperor's advisers, concerned above all with keeping her faction in position. She negotiates with Shai from a position of total power and makes no pretence otherwise.
characters.name: Frava

characters.description: Emperor of the Rose Empire. An assassination attempt left his body physically repaired but his mind destroyed: he breathes and can be moved, and nothing of the man is left. His arbiters have concealed the truth of his condition, because an emperor who cannot rule would mean the end of their council.
characters.name: Emperor Ashravan

characters.description: The general on the arbiters' council, a blunt soldier with no patience for the politics of the palace and no enthusiasm for the arrangement the council has made with a condemned criminal.
characters.name: Han ShuXen

characters.description: The captain of the guards assigned to watch Shai. He regards her as a criminal who was already sentenced and should already be dead, and he does not hide that he would prefer to carry the sentence out himself.
characters.name: Captain Zu

characters.description: A practitioner of a cruder, blood-based magic, hired to seal Shai's room each day with a mark keyed to her own blood so that she cannot leave it. He is careless, unpleasant and resented by everyone involved, and the seal has to be renewed daily, which is the one constraint on Shai that her own art cannot simply rewrite.
characters.name: The Bloodsealer

recaps.ending: Shai finishes the soul stamp within her hundred days and it works: applied to Ashravan, it restores him to himself, and the arbiters keep their emperor, though the stamp will have to be renewed indefinitely for the rest of his life. She has written one deliberate change into him, restoring the drive to leave the empire better than he found it that the real man had abandoned years earlier. Knowing that Frava intends to have her killed once the work is delivered, Shai escapes on her own schedule, recovering the possessions the council confiscated, including the alternate versions of herself she spent years creating, and taking with her the genuine artefact she had been convicted of stealing, leaving the palace holding her forgery of it. Gaotona, who began by calling her a thief, is left with the argument settled against him: among the work she leaves behind is a stamp of her own soul, and it demonstrates plainly that what she does is art. The empire's rulers keep their secret and their emperor, Shai keeps her freedom and her prize, and the two of them part with a mutual respect neither expected.
recaps.in_short: Shai, a Forger who can rewrite an object's history by carving a stamp that reality will accept, is caught in the palace of the Rose Empire after swapping a priceless artefact for a copy of her own making. Forgery is a capital crime there, but before she can be executed the emperor's arbiters offer a bargain: an assassination attempt has left Emperor Ashravan's body intact and his mind gone, and they want her to forge a stamp that will recreate his soul. She has a hundred days, a sealed room and guards who would rather kill her. Working from the imperial records and arguing about art with the elderly arbiter Gaotona, she reconstructs a whole man accurately enough for his own body to accept the result, while quietly preparing her escape. The stamp works and Ashravan is restored, with one change she wrote in deliberately. Shai escapes with her confiscated possessions and the real artefact, leaving Gaotona convinced that Forgery is art rather than fraud.

recaps.text: Shai, a Forger from MaiPon, is caught in the palace of the Rose Empire after swapping a priceless imperial artefact for a forgery of her own. Forgery, the art of carving a stamp that rewrites an object's history so convincingly that reality accepts the new version, is a capital crime in the empire, and she is imprisoned to await execution. Instead of killing her, the emperor's arbiters put an offer to her: an assassination attempt has left Emperor Ashravan's body physically intact but his mind destroyed, and the council, which would lose everything if he were replaced, wants Shai to forge a stamp that will restore his soul. She is given a hundred days, a locked room, guards who would rather see her dead, and access to the imperial records.

Shai accepts, on her own terms, and starts work. Forging a soul means reconstructing an entire life accurately enough that the man's own body will accept the result, so she reads everything the empire has ever recorded about Ashravan and has to understand him better than his friends did. Gaotona, the oldest and most rigid of the arbiters, is assigned to review her drafts and treats the whole business as a criminal performing a trick. Her room is sealed each day by a blood-based magic keyed to her own blood, so ordinary escape is impossible, and Frava, who leads the council, plainly has no intention of letting her live once the commission is delivered. Shai therefore prepares her escape alongside the work, forging small changes into her surroundings that nobody thinks to look for.

The work advances through successive drafts. Shai learns Ashravan as a young man, his ambitions, his marriage, his failures, and the point at which he stopped trying to reform the empire and settled for holding it, and she has to decide what to do about everything the official record leaves out. Gaotona's contempt gradually becomes interest as he watches her build versions of the emperor's soul and reject them for reasons he can follow and eventually anticipate. Meanwhile the palace's factions manoeuvre around the secret they are all keeping, the guard captain watches her constantly, and the daily blood seal remains the one thing standing between her and the door.

With the deadline closing, the problem stops being technical and becomes a question of what a soul is for. A stamp accurate enough to work would reproduce a man who had already given up, and Shai has to decide whether to recreate Ashravan exactly or to correct him. She and Gaotona argue about whether Forgery is art or theft, and he concedes more ground than he means to. On the other side, Frava's intentions for Shai once the stamp is delivered become explicit enough that her escape has to be finished on exactly the same schedule as the emperor's soul.

Shai completes the stamp and it works: applied to Ashravan it restores him to himself, and the empire keeps its emperor, though the stamp will need renewing for as long as he lives. She has written one deliberate change into him, a renewed determination to leave the empire better than he found it, which is the thing the original man had given up. Anticipating Frava's plan to have her killed on delivery, she escapes on her own terms, recovering the possessions the council had confiscated, including the alternate versions of herself she had spent years making, and taking the genuine artefact she was convicted of stealing while the palace keeps her forgery of it. Gaotona is left with proof of what she is: among the work she abandons is a stamp of her own soul, which settles their argument in her favour.

characters.description: The Banu Nahida of Daevabad, thrown out of the city she had spent five years learning to survive and washed up in the country she was born in. She knows now that Banu Manizheh is her mother, that Jamshid is her brother, and that the woman who bore her has just taken Daevabad by poisoning a festival. She has no magic worth the name outside the city's walls, no army, and a very long habit of solving problems by lying to the right person.
characters.name: Nahri

characters.description: The surviving Qahtani prince, carrying Suleiman's seal in his heart and the marid's work in his body. His father is dead, his brother is dying in a captured palace, and the magic that saved his life is steadily making him into something the djinn have no comfortable name for. Stranded in Egypt with Nahri, he is the reason Daevabad has no magic, and he cannot go back without carrying the one thing his father's killers still need straight to them.
characters.name: Alizayd

characters.description: The Afshin, raised from the dead to win Manizheh a city and having now done it. He destroyed the Citadel, delivered the army that made the massacre possible, and is left occupying a conquered Daevabad in the name of a Banu Nahida whose orders he can no longer pretend are defensible. Bound to her service and to fourteen centuries of doing what he was told, he is a soldier with nothing left to tell himself.
characters.name: Dara

characters.description: The Nahid healer who spent twenty years presumed dead and has now taken Daevabad, at the cost of most of its Geziri population. She rules a city whose magic died the moment the seal-bearer fled it, holds the emir hostage, and intends to put her son Jamshid on the throne. Nahri's mother, and entirely unmoved by what that is supposed to mean.
characters.name: Manizheh

characters.description: Kaveh's son and, as of the fall of Daevabad, publicly Banu Manizheh's son and Nahri's half-brother. A Nahid who spent his whole life believing he had no magic at all, he is now the heir his mother wants and the only healer who can keep Muntadhir alive, which is precisely how she keeps him cooperative.
characters.name: Jamshid

characters.description: Emir of Daevabad, mortally wounded in the taking of the city and kept alive in a captured palace because his survival is useful to the people holding it. His father is dead, his brother and his wife are gone, and the man he loves is the son of the woman who did all of it.
characters.name: Muntadhir

characters.description: Ghassan's daughter, who survived the massacre and is left in an occupied city with no title anyone will honour and no intention of sitting still. She is the most politically able of her family and the only Qahtani still inside Daevabad's walls with any freedom of movement.
characters.name: Zaynab

characters.description: Former grand wazir of Daevabad, Manizheh's oldest collaborator and the man who released the poison that killed the Geziri. He is Jamshid's father, and he has spent decades believing that everything he did was for his tribe and for his son.
characters.name: Kaveh

characters.description: Ali's mother, an Ayaanle noblewoman of Ta Ntry, who survived the poison because it was not made for her tribe. She has family, money and standing in a wealthy country far from Daevabad, and a son who has just become the most dangerous person alive to shelter.
characters.name: Hatset

characters.description: An ifrit allied to Manizheh, one of the original daevas who refused Suleiman's judgement. He has been circling the Nahid family for a very long time, and the price he expects for his help was agreed before the war began.
characters.name: Aeshma

characters.description: The elderly Cairo apothecary Nahri worked beside before she was taken east, still in the same shop, still convinced she takes too many risks. He is the only person in the world who knew her before any of this.
characters.name: Yaqub

characters.description: A marid of the Nile, ancient and territorial, bound by an old pact to the Ayaanle line Ali is descended from. He speaks in obligations rather than affection, and what he is owed and what he owes are not the same thing.
characters.name: Sobek

characters.description: A shafit ship's captain, quick, mercenary and completely unimpressed by djinn nobility. She joins Nahri and Ali's expedition on terms she negotiates herself and holds them to.
characters.name: Fiza

characters.description: The eldest of the marid, vast and ancient, who holds the sea and the memory of every bargain her kind ever made. The marid's grievance against Daevabad is older than the Qahtanis and older than the Nahid dynasty, and she is not inclined to be helpful about it.
characters.name: Tiamat

recaps.ending: The trilogy closes with Manizheh's defeat. Dara turns on the woman who raised him from the dead rather than carry out the last of what she asks, and Manizheh is killed in the final confrontation for Daevabad. Ali is very nearly killed in it and survives only through marid intervention, which leaves him permanently altered. Nahri, holding the power that three books of characters have fought and murdered to control, declines to keep it: rather than take Suleiman's seal for herself and rule as her ancestors ruled, she ends the arrangement that placed absolute magical authority in one person's hands, and Daevabad's magic returns to the city and to its people. What follows is not a restoration of the Nahid dynasty. Daevabad is left to be governed jointly, with the shafit represented for the first time in its history rather than confined, and with the surviving Qahtanis, Nahri and Jamshid sharing the work of holding it together. Muntadhir survives and is healed at last of the wound that had been killing him. Jamshid takes up the place among the Daeva that his parentage gives him. Nahri does not become queen: she takes the hospital she rebuilt and the practice she wanted from the first chapter of the first book, with Ali beside her. Dara survives, freed of the magic that made him someone else's weapon, and is left to answer for what he did while he was one.
recaps.in_short: Daevabad has fallen to Banu Manizheh and lost its magic, and Nahri and Alizayd are stranded in Egypt with Suleiman's seal and no way home. Hiding in Cairo, they are hunted by Manizheh's allies; guided by Sobek, an ancient marid bound to Ali's family line, they escape to Ta Ntry, where Ali's mother Hatset shelters them and where they uncover how Daevabad was really founded and what the Nahids and the marid did to build it. Nahri learns that she is Manizheh's daughter by a human father, which makes the champion of the shafit shafit herself. In occupied Daevabad, Muntadhir is kept alive as leverage over Jamshid, whom Manizheh means to make her heir, while Dara, sickened by what he has done and by what Manizheh has promised the ifrit, begins to break with her. Nahri and Ali return with allies and a bargain struck with the marid. Manizheh is defeated and killed, Ali is nearly killed and permanently changed, and Nahri ends the seal's absolute power rather than claim it, restoring Daevabad's magic and leaving the city to be governed jointly, shafit included.

recaps.text: Previously, in the Daevabad trilogy: Nahri, a con artist in Ottoman Cairo, discovered she carried the blood of the Nahids, the healer family that once ruled the hidden djinn city of Daevabad, and was brought there by Darayavahoush the Afshin. The city had been taken from the Nahids fourteen centuries earlier by the Qahtanis, who rule its six tribes and confine the part-human shafit to poverty. King Ghassan installed Nahri in his palace as Banu Nahida and married her to his heir Muntadhir; she became friends with his younger son Alizayd, who was exiled to the desert after his secret support for a shafit organization was exposed. Dara was killed on the city's lake by a marid-possessed Ali, and raised again by Banu Manizheh, the Nahid healer everyone believed dead for twenty years, who is Nahri's mother. Five years later Manizheh took Daevabad during the Navasatem festival: Dara destroyed the Citadel while the grand wazir Kaveh released a poison that killed the city's Geziri, King Ghassan among them. Muntadhir was left mortally wounded, Kaveh revealed that Jamshid is his son by Manizheh and therefore Nahri's half-brother, and Nahri finally met her mother. Suleiman's seal passed to Ali, who escaped into the lake with Nahri and surfaced in the Nile. With the seal-bearer gone from the island, Daevabad's magic went out entirely, leaving Manizheh in possession of a broken city and Nahri and Ali stranded in Egypt.

Nahri and Ali come ashore on the Nile with no magic, no money and no way back. Ali is carrying Suleiman's seal and the marid's changes to his body, and neither is behaving the way anyone expected. Nahri is home for the first time in years, in a Cairo that has moved on without her, and she is not entirely sorry about it. Far to the east, Daevabad has stopped working: the wards are down, conjured things have failed, the sick cannot be healed by magic, and Manizheh rules a city of terrified survivors by force alone. Muntadhir is kept alive in the palace because his life is what makes Jamshid cooperative, and Dara, who won the city for her, is discovering what occupying it actually requires of him.

Hiding in Cairo, Nahri returns to the apothecary Yaqub and to the work she did before any of this, treating human patients with human medicine, and finds she is better at that life than she wants to admit. Ali is a conspicuous problem: he cannot pass for human, the seal in his chest is a beacon, and the water keeps answering him. Manizheh's reach extends further than Egypt, and the pair are found. In Daevabad, Manizheh consolidates: she disposes of anyone who resists, presses Jamshid toward the throne she intends him to take, and keeps Muntadhir alive by inches. Dara's objections to her methods begin to be objections rather than misgivings, and she does not take them well.

Ali's marid inheritance turns out to have a name and an owner. Sobek, an ancient marid of the Nile, is bound by an old pact to the Ayaanle line Ali descends from, and his help comes framed entirely as debts and obligations. With his intervention Nahri and Ali get out of Egypt and cross to Ta Ntry, the Ayaanle homeland on the far side of the sea, where Hatset takes them in. Ta Ntry is wealthy, undamaged and full of people with opinions about what a Qahtani prince who cannot bleed properly is now good for. Nahri, who has spent two books being told what she is by people who benefit from the answer, starts asking her own questions about where the Nahids' power actually came from.

In Ta Ntry, the founding story of Daevabad comes apart. The version every tribe has been taught, in which Suleiman rewarded the Nahids with the seal and Anahid built the brass city as a refuge, leaves out how the city was actually raised and who was compelled to raise it. The marid's grievance against Daevabad turns out to be very old and very specific, and it explains a great deal about the lake, its curse, and what happened to Ali in it. Nahri and Ali begin assembling something like a plan and something like an alliance, drawing in the Ayaanle and the shafit, including a ship's captain named Fiza who is willing to be paid for the risk. In Daevabad, Zaynab and the survivors organize what resistance a magicless occupied city allows.

Nahri learns the truth about herself. Manizheh bore her in Egypt, to a human father, and hid what that meant: the Banu Nahida who fought to open a hospital to the shafit is shafit herself, the exact thing her mother's faction holds in contempt. Dara, meanwhile, learns the rest of his own history, including how the Nahids he served used him and what was done to him and his family afterwards, and he learns what Manizheh has actually promised the ifrit in exchange for their help. The bargain involves djinn souls, and it is not a price he is willing to see paid. Manizheh's response to being questioned is to remind him what he is bound by, and Dara begins looking for the seam in it.

Restoring Daevabad's magic means dealing with the marid on the marid's terms, which means going to the eldest of them, Tiamat, who remembers the original offence and has waited a very long time to collect on it. The bargain that comes out of it is expensive, and Ali pays most of it. With a marid agreement, an Ayaanle-backed force and a shafit fleet, Nahri and Ali turn back toward the city, knowing that the seal Ali carries is the one thing Manizheh cannot take Daevabad's magic back without, and that bringing it home means bringing it within her reach.

The return to Daevabad begins. The lake, the veil and the ruined defences all behave differently in a city with no magic, and the assault does not go to anyone's plan. Manizheh has been waiting for exactly this, because it delivers the seal to her doorstep, and the fighting inside the city turns on which of the Nahids, Qahtanis and Afshins present will do what they have been told. Dara's break with Manizheh becomes open. Jamshid, Muntadhir and Zaynab are forced to act from inside the palace rather than around it, and Nahri arrives at the confrontation with her mother that the whole trilogy has been arranging.

The last battle for Daevabad settles everything. Dara turns on Manizheh rather than carry out the last of what she asks of him, and Manizheh is killed. Ali is nearly killed as well and survives only through marid intervention, which leaves him permanently changed. Nahri finishes holding what everyone has been fighting for and refuses to keep it: instead of taking Suleiman's seal and ruling as her ancestors did, she ends the arrangement that put absolute magical authority into a single pair of hands, and Daevabad's magic comes back to the city and to everyone in it. The Nahid dynasty is not restored, the Qahtani monarchy is not restored, and the shafit are not put back behind their walls.

In the epilogue, Daevabad is rebuilding under a shared government in which the shafit are represented for the first time, with the surviving Qahtanis, Nahri and Jamshid all carrying part of the work. Muntadhir has been healed of the wound that was killing him. Jamshid takes up the position among the Daeva that his parentage gives him. Nahri does not take a throne; she takes the hospital she rebuilt and the practice she wanted from the beginning, with Ali beside her. Dara is alive and unbound, facing what he did with fourteen centuries of obedience behind him and nobody left to give him orders.

characters.description: The Earth-born innkeeper of the Wandering Inn. She has made a home near Liscor and protects the varied people who gather there.
characters.name: Erin Solstice

characters.description: A young Gnoll who lives under the protection of Erin, Lyonette, and the inn's wider household.
characters.name: Mrsha

characters.description: Liscor's Watch Captain, responsible for the imprisoned Minotaur.
characters.name: Zevara

characters.description: An imprisoned Minotaur commander held under Zevara's lawful authority in Liscor.
characters.name: Calruz

characters.description: An inventive necromancer and member of the Horns.
characters.name: Pisces

characters.description: The half-elf leader and ice mage of the Horns, an adventuring team based around Liscor.
characters.name: Ceria Springwalker

characters.description: An adventurer and member of the Horns.
characters.name: Yvlon

characters.description: The Antinium adventurer in the Horns.
characters.name: Ksmvr

characters.description: A Goblin survivor who lives at the Wandering Inn under Erin's protection.
characters.name: Numbtongue

characters.description: A manager of the Wandering Inn and one of Mrsha's guardians.
characters.name: Lyonette

characters.description: A damaged, sentient skeleton confined to Liscor's mana-rich dungeon. Toren also moves through a masked female form and, burdened by abandoning Erin, has begun choosing to protect living beings.
characters.name: Toren

characters.description: A former-miner adventuring team led by Erlea. Its members recover valuable materials by dismantling inactive traps in Liscor's dungeon.
characters.name: Gemhammer

characters.description: Anith's silver-rank adventuring team. They guard Gemhammer's salvage work and regard the dungeon's masked warrior as a benefactor.
characters.name: Vuleil Dre

characters.description: The gold-rank Wings of Pallass are commanded by Bavusa. She questions the identity of a masked dungeon combatant, but relents when she understands the figure's behavior around a destroyed zombie as mourning.
characters.name: Bavusa

characters.description: An intelligent black skeleton created as one of a necromancer's Chosen. After a failed attack on Zel Shivertail, she waits for new orders and fears her creator has abandoned her.
characters.name: Black skeleton

characters.description: Liscor's strategist and the administrative guide for its newly seated council, helping the inexperienced body turn its proposed reforms into policy.
characters.name: Olesm

characters.description: An armorer chosen for Liscor's new Gnoll council. Her trade plan would send ore from Esselm to Pallass in return for metal goods and instruction for local smiths.
characters.name: Regrika

characters.description: A Liscor resident entrusted with the Heartflame armor.
characters.name: Selys

characters.description: An officer of Liscor's Watch.
characters.name: Relc

characters.description: The Wall Lord of Salazsar. He gave Erin a family ring protected by an enchantment that makes it easy to overlook, and he secretly shelters a surviving Pallasian captain.
characters.name: Ilvriss

characters.description: A military survivor and the niece of a dead Pallasian general. Ilvriss conceals her identity, presents her as his bodyguard, and entrusts her with organizing a covert force.
characters.name: Pallasian captain

characters.description: An undead former human archmage ruling a concealed castle west of the Bloodfields. He commands an army, specialized Chosen, and distant puppets, and has begun teaching Pisces through an undead rat.
characters.name: Hidden necromancer

characters.description: The ruler of a beast-taming empire under coalition invasion. She directs war elephants and other animal-supported defenders while the enemy closes around her capital.
characters.name: Empress of Beasts

characters.description: An unnamed correspondent whose unusually detailed accounts from the war front place the reporter at risk. A magic academy sends a team to find and recover the correspondent.
characters.name: Unnamed frontline reporter

characters.description: A distant monarch whose peace proclamation limits his response to the war against the Empress. With her capital surrounded, she asks him to decide her empire's fate.
characters.name: Flos

characters.description: The elected leader of a golem-state in the coalition. He remains at the front despite expecting a devastating final assault and prepares his command for the possibility of his death.
characters.name: Magus-crafter

characters.description: Commander of the defeated empire's remaining field army. During the surrender, the general leads soldiers and civilians north toward the Kaleel Steppes.
characters.name: Empress's general

characters.description: Germina's child ruler, carrying the memories and knowledge of earlier Quarasses despite the limited magic and strength of her present body. She allies with Flos to protect her country.
characters.name: Quarass of Germina

characters.description: An Earth-born envoy traveling on Flos's behalf. He explains his world's technology to the Quarass and accompanies her into negotiations with Kelt.
characters.name: Trey

characters.description: Kelt's ancient ruler and guardian. He withdraws his army while talks proceed, but demands lasting safeguards before aiding a conqueror whose reign he considers temporary.
characters.name: Kelt's undead king

characters.description: A smallfolk strategist, professor, and second-in-command of a great mercenary company. He uses live deceptions to test his advanced students and expects them to challenge authority as well as master logistics.
characters.name: Niers Astoragon

characters.description: A stealth specialist who leads Niers's mercenary company. She can pass unnoticed at close range and selectively remove memories.
characters.name: Head of Niers's company

characters.description: One of Niers's unconventional students, strong at tactical surprise but still developing the authority and appetite for risk needed for larger commands.
characters.name: Lizardfolk strategist student

characters.description: A strategist student with a gift for logistics and a direct approach to command. Family duty competes with his private wish to pursue a great discovery.
characters.name: Human lord student

characters.description: The leader of five Wistram mages and a former associate of Pisces and Ceria. She forcibly detains Pisces and the Horns without first consulting Liscor's Watch.
characters.name: Wistram team leader

characters.description: One of the five Wistram mages who participates in the team's unsanctioned seizure of Pisces and the Horns.
characters.name: Wistram team mage

characters.description: Pisces's full identity, revealed when he admits his common-born Terandrian upbringing and accepts responsibility for the fatal Wistram tomb theft. He refuses surrender, and the Horns reaffirm their loyalty to him.
characters.name: Pisces Jilnet

recaps.ending:
The Empress of Beasts survives by surrendering and remains a political prisoner of the magus-crafter as coalition powers divide her former realm. Her general escapes north with soldiers and civilians, preserving an armed resistance, and Flos still owes the Empress the restoration he promised. Immediate war between Kelt and Rhyme is avoided through a provisional exchange of grain for Flos's blood oath of nonaggression.

In Liscor, Wistram's attempt to seize Pisces and the Horns ends in defeat and arrest. Pisces is freed and treated, then acknowledges his full name, common-born past, and responsibility for the fatal tomb incident at Wistram. The Horns remain united around him. Wistram's leader departs determined to capture both Pisces and Erin, and a large bounty leaves their allies exposed. Toren remains concealed in the dungeon, Ilvriss's anti-necromancer force is still forming, and the hidden necromancer continues to observe the inn and test Pisces from afar.
recaps.in_short: Toren struggles toward a protective purpose while trapped in Liscor's dungeon, and Ilvriss quietly prepares to fight a surviving necromancer who has begun mentoring Pisces. Abroad, the Empress of Beasts surrenders rather than sacrifice her people, losing her realm and becoming the magus-crafter's prisoner while her general escapes with an army. Flos promises eventual restoration and averts war with Kelt through a provisional food-for-nonaggression pact. Niers Astoragon learns that dragons remain hidden on Izril and suspects a connection between his chess opponent and Liscor. Wistram mages abduct Pisces and the Horns, but Erin's household and allies defeat them. Pisces admits that he is Pisces Jilnet and that his attempted tomb theft caused deaths at Wistram. The Horns stand by him, while Wistram leaves him under a large bounty and marks Erin as another target.

recaps.text: Previously: Erin Solstice, an innkeeper from Earth, established the Wandering Inn near Liscor and gathered an unusual household around it. Mrsha lives there under the care of Erin and Lyonette, while the Goblin survivor Numbtongue is also protected at the inn. The adventuring team known as the Horns includes the necromancer Pisces, the half-elf ice mage Ceria Springwalker, Yvlon, and the Antinium Ksmvr. Calruz, a Minotaur commander, is imprisoned under Watch Captain Zevara's authority. These relationships leave the inn closely tied to Liscor's civic life, its adventurers, and people whom other powers regard with suspicion.

Toren is trapped in Liscor's dungeon, where abundant mana repairs his damaged undead body but the surface cannot sustain him. His efforts to command other undead fail against stronger creatures, yet he begins protecting living explorers and recognizes his regret over abandoning Erin. Adventurers know his masked female form only as a helpful dungeon warrior. After an undead assault, they cremate the zombie Toren had dressed to resemble Erin and mistake his attachment for grief.

Liscor's newly seated council begins rent, trade, Watch, and Antinium reforms. Erin receives citizenship, pays reduced back taxes, and learns that Ilvriss's plain family ring carries an enchantment that discourages notice. In Salazsar, Ilvriss secretly shelters a surviving Pallasian captain and starts assembling an elite force against the necromancer under the cover of anti-Antinium preparations.

Pisces privately develops a large bone construct and receives instruction through an undead rat.
